subject: RFP: commercial/pricing clarifications - consumption accelerator credit waterfall & commit transitions
messages:
From: Alice Hart <alice.hart@greenlinebank.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Evans <tom.evans@vendorops.greenlinebank.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFP clarifications: commercial appendix - consumption behavior and commits

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the RFP materials. Procurement and Vendor Ops reviewed the commercial appendix and we have a couple of clarifications before we score your response: 

1) The "accelerator credit waterfall" you propose for pilot-to-prod ramp — can you confirm whether unused accelerator credits roll forward into the next quarter or expire at quarter end? We need a clean audit trail for finance.

2) For commit transitions (pilot -> committed annual), clarify how per-token rates change mid-quarter if we convert a portion of usage into a committed bucket. Is pricing pro-rated or do you apply a retroactive true-up?

3) Overages: your ladder shows stepped unit pricing after commit thresholds. Can you confirm whether overage caps or soft-limits are available (e.g., gracebands), and how notifications are delivered to our billing/ops teams?

Attached: the RFP commercial appendix with line numbers (we referenced rows 23-41).

Can we get a written clarification and an updated appendix by next Wednesday (3/3)?

Thanks,

Alice Hart
Sr. Procurement Manager
GreenLine Bank

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Hart <alice.hart@greenlinebank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP clarifications: commercial appendix - consumption behavior and commits

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear line references, that helps. Responses below and an attached updated pricing appendix (v2) for you to drop into the RFP spreadsheet. High-level answers:  

1) Accelerator credits: expire at quarter end by default (to keep accounting clean). However, for pilots converting to a committed contract we offer a one-time roll-forward of unused accelerator credits into the first month of the committed term (documented in the SOW). That roll-forward is captured as an invoice-level credit and appears as a separate line item (no re-pricing of prior usage).

2) Commit transitions: we apply a forward-looking pro-rate on the remaining billing period. We do not retroactively change per-token rates on already-invoiced usage. Example: if you convert 60% of anticipated monthly usage to a committed bucket mid-quarter, you receive committed unit pricing on the committed volume for the remainder of that billing cycle; previously invoiced non-committed usage remains billed at the non-committed rate with a true-up credit applied only in the scenario where the annual true-up reduces your overall invoice (we show this in the appendix with a sample compute).

3) Overages & gracebands: we support a configurable graceband (default 10% of commit) where overage is billed at a soft-rate (midpoint between committed rate and list overage rate) for the first tolerance window. Notifications can be pushed via email + webhook to your billing/ops webhook endpoint; we also provide daily usage CSV exports and an API to query rolling 7/30/90-day consumption.

I've highlighted the above items in the attached PDF and added a worked example on rows 58-64. If the team wants different expiry semantics for accelerator credits (e.g., multi-quarter roll-forward), we'll need to expose that as a negotiated term in the SOW with modest commercial impact.

I'll loop Ben for confirmation on discounting flex.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-pricing-appendix-v2.pdf

Hi Alice / Tom — attaching the revised commercial appendix (v2) and a short worked example for a mid-quarter conversion and a 1-month accelerator roll-forward. Summary of updates included inline: 

• Accelerator credits: default expire EOM; one-time 1-month roll-forward for pilot->committed transitions (no retroactive price changes; credit shown as invoice line).
• Commit transitions: forward-looking pro-rate on remainder of billing period; no retroactive re-pricing of recorded invoices. Annual true-up can generate invoice credits where applicable (see worked example).
• Overages & graceband: default 10% graceband at enterprise tier; optional 15% at Gold band; first-notice via email + webhook; daily exports & usage API available.

Please confirm if you'd like us to make the accelerator roll-forward 2 months instead of 1 month (note: that will require a modest unit-price concession). Attached files: 2026-02-24-GreenLine-RFP-commercial-appendix.xlsx and redwood-pricing-appendix-v2.pdf.

Thanks,
Jasmine

Hi Jasmine/Ben — thanks for the rapid turnaround and for codifying the examples. Procurement's commercial scoring team reviewed v2 and had two quick follow-ups before we mark you as "compliant":

A) For the 1-month roll-forward, please confirm the exact invoice flow (we want the credit to be applied as a separate line with a reference to the original pilot invoice id and the new committed SOW id). Can you provide the invoice example language you intend to use?

B) For overage notifications, we'd prefer a webhook that posts to our internal-billing endpoint (https://events.greenlinebank.internal/billing/usage). Can you confirm Redwood can deliver notifications to that endpoint (mutual TLS available) and include a sample JSON payload structure?

If you can provide those two items by EOD Friday (3/6) we'll proceed. Appreciate the clarity — pricing appendix looks good otherwise.

Best,
